title: Confirmed black holes vs. the estimated total in the Milky Way

source.name: 2017 stellar-mass black hole census of the Milky Way

notes: UC Irvine astronomers estimated in 2017 that the Milky Way holds roughly 100 million stellar-mass black holes, based on how many massive stars the galaxy has formed over its history (about 1 in 1,000 stars is massive enough to collapse into one). Combined light- and gravitational-wave detections had confirmed roughly 400 individual black holes as of the 2026 GWTC-5.0 catalog.
